question: How many 5-element subsets of {1, 2, ..., 15} contain at least one multiple of 4 and at least one multiple of 6?
error_description: In the 'neither' term of inclusion-exclusion, the excluded elements are counted as 3 multiples of 4 plus 2 multiples of 6 = 5, counting 12 twice; this gives C(10,5) = 252 instead of C(11,5) = 462, so the total becomes 3003 - 792 - 1287 + 252 = 1176.
solution: The multiples of 4 are {4,8,12} and the multiples of 6 are {6,12}; note 12 belongs to both, so their union is {4,6,8,12} with 4 elements. By inclusion-exclusion, the count is (all 5-subsets) - (those with no multiple of 4) - (those with no multiple of 6) + (those with neither). All: C(15,5) = 3003. No multiple of 4: choose from the other 12 numbers, C(12,5) = 792. No multiple of 6: C(13,5) = 1287. Neither: choose from the 15 - 4 = 11 numbers outside the union, C(11,5) = 462. Answer: 3003 - 792 - 1287 + 462 = 1386.
